title: Judges Chapter 6 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Judges chapter 6 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Judges Chapter 6 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Judges Chapter 6.

questions.question: How many years did the LORD deliver Israel into the hand of Midian?
questions.correctAnswer: Seven years
questions.explanation: Judges 6:1 states that the LORD delivered Israel into the hand of Midian for seven years.

questions.question: Where did the children of Israel make their dens to hide from the Midianites?
questions.correctAnswer: Mountains, caves, and strong holds
questions.explanation: Judges 6:2 explains that Israel made dens in the mountains, caves, and strong holds because of the Midianites.

questions.question: Who came up against Israel when they had sown their crops?
options: Midianites, Amalekites, and children of the east
questions.correctAnswer: Midianites, Amalekites, and children of the east
questions.explanation: Judges 6:3 states that the Midianites, Amalekites, and children of the east came up against Israel after they had sown.

questions.question: True or False: The Midianites left ample food and livestock for Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 6:4 states the Midianites left no sustenance for Israel, neither sheep, ox, nor ass.

questions.question: The multitude of the Midianites and their camels is compared to what?
questions.correctAnswer: Grasshoppers
questions.explanation: Judges 6:5 compares the multitude of the Midianites and their camels to grasshoppers for their vast number.

questions.question: What was Israel's condition because of the Midianites?
questions.correctAnswer: Greatly impoverished
questions.explanation: Judges 6:6 states that Israel was greatly impoverished because of the Midianites.

questions.question: True or False: When Israel cried unto the LORD because of the Midianites, He ignored their cries.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 6:7-8 shows that when Israel cried unto the LORD, He sent a prophet to them, indicating He did not ignore them.

questions.question: What did the LORD say He had done for Israel in the prophet's message?
options: Brought them up from Egypt and delivered them
Made them kings over other nations
questions.correctAnswer: Brought them up from Egypt and delivered them
questions.explanation: Judges 6:8-9 recount that the LORD said He brought Israel up from Egypt, delivered them from oppression, and gave them their land.

questions.question: Who was threshing wheat by the winepress to hide it from the Midianites?
questions.correctAnswer: Gideon
questions.explanation: Judges 6:11 states that Gideon, son of Joash, was threshing wheat by the winepress to hide it from the Midianites.

questions.question: True or False: The angel of the LORD called Gideon 'mighty man of valour.'
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 6:12 records the angel of the LORD greeting Gideon as 'thou mighty man of valour.'

questions.question: What was Gideon's response when the angel said the LORD was with him?
options: He questioned why all these troubles had come upon Israel
He immediately accepted the message without doubt
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned why all these troubles had come upon Israel
questions.explanation: Judges 6:13 shows Gideon questioning why Israel had suffered and where God's miracles were if the LORD was with them.

questions.question: What command did the LORD give to Gideon after looking upon him?
options: Go in thy might and save Israel from Midian
Flee and hide from the Midianites
questions.correctAnswer: Go in thy might and save Israel from Midian
questions.explanation: Judges 6:14 records the LORD's command to Gideon to go in his might and save Israel from the Midianites.

questions.question: True or False: Gideon told the LORD that he was the least in his father's house and his family was poor.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 6:15 shows Gideon expressing his low status and poverty in his family when questioning how he could save Israel.

questions.question: In Judges 6, which instruction comes before all the others listed here?
options: Build an altar unto the LORD upon the rock
Throw down the altar of Baal
Offer a burnt sacrifice with the wood of the grove
questions.correctAnswer: Take thy father's young bullock
questions.explanation: Judges 6:25 instructs Gideon first to take his father's young bullock before throwing down the altar of Baal or performing other actions.

questions.question: What did the LORD promise Gideon regarding his mission to save Israel?
options: Surely I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite Midianites as one man
You will become king of Israel
questions.correctAnswer: Surely I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite Midianites as one man
questions.explanation: Judges 6:16 records the LORD's promise to Gideon that He would be with him and he would defeat the Midianites as one man.

medium.title: Judges Chapter 6 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Judges Chapter 6 to real-life situations.

questions.question: How did Gideon initially react to the angel of the LORD's greeting calling him a mighty man of valour?
options: He accepted the compliment and prepared for battle
He questioned why Israel had suffered and doubted God's presence
He immediately obeyed the LORD's command
He fled to hide from the Midianites
questions.correctAnswer: He questioned why Israel had suffered and doubted God's presence
questions.explanation: Judges 6:12-13 shows Gideon responding with doubt, asking why all the suffering had come upon Israel if the LORD was truly with them, reflecting his uncertainty despite the angel's encouragement.

questions.question: What promise did the LORD give to Gideon to assure him of success against the Midianites?
options: He would fight the Midianites Himself
He would be with Gideon and he would smite the Midianites as one man
He would provide weapons for Gideon
questions.correctAnswer: He would be with Gideon and he would smite the Midianites as one man
questions.explanation: In Judges 6:16, the LORD promises to be with Gideon and that he will defeat the Midianites as if he were one man, assuring Gideon of divine support despite his initial fears in verse 15.

questions.question: Why did Gideon ask the angel of the LORD for a sign?
options: To be sure he was speaking with a man
To confirm the LORD's presence and message
questions.correctAnswer: To confirm the LORD's presence and message
questions.explanation: Judges 6:17 reveals Gideon's request for a sign to confirm that the angel was truly sent by God, showing his need for reassurance before acting.

questions.question: What did Gideon prepare to offer to the angel of the LORD as a present?
options: A kid and unleavened cakes with broth
questions.correctAnswer: A kid and unleavened cakes with broth
questions.explanation: According to Judges 6:19, Gideon prepared a kid and unleavened cakes of flour, placing the flesh in a basket and the broth in a pot to present to the angel under the oak.

questions.question: What miraculous sign did the angel of the LORD perform with the flesh and unleavened cakes?
options: Made them float in the air
Fire rose out of the rock and consumed them
They multiplied to feed many people
questions.correctAnswer: Fire rose out of the rock and consumed them
questions.explanation: Judges 6:21 describes the angel touching the flesh and unleavened cakes with his staff, causing fire to rise from the rock and consume them, confirming the divine presence to Gideon.

questions.question: What was Gideon's reaction after perceiving the angel of the LORD?
options: He said, 'Alas, O Lord GOD! for because I have seen an angel of the LORD face to face'
questions.correctAnswer: He said, 'Alas, O Lord GOD! for because I have seen an angel of the LORD face to face'
questions.explanation: Judges 6:22 shows Gideon expressing fear and awe because he had seen the angel of the LORD face to face, which was a terrifying experience for him.

questions.question: What name did Gideon give to the altar he built after his encounter with the angel?
questions.correctAnswer: Jehovah Shalom
questions.explanation: Judges 6:24 records that Gideon built an altar called Jehovahshalom, meaning 'The LORD is Peace', symbolizing God's peace with him despite his earlier fear.

questions.question: What specific task did the LORD command Gideon to do regarding his father's altar and the grove?
options: Build another altar next to them
Throw down the altar of Baal and cut down the grove
Offer a sacrifice on the existing altar
questions.correctAnswer: Throw down the altar of Baal and cut down the grove
questions.explanation: In Judges 6:25, God instructs Gideon to destroy the altar of Baal and the grove beside it, indicating a call to reject idolatry and restore true worship.

questions.question: Why did Gideon perform the destruction of the altar and grove at night?
options: Because it was the sacred time for sacrifices
Because he feared his father's household and the men of the city
Because the angel of the LORD told him to
questions.correctAnswer: Because he feared his father's household and the men of the city
questions.explanation: Judges 6:27 explains that Gideon did the work by night due to fear of his family and neighbors, showing his cautious obedience amid potential opposition.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the men of the city when they found the altar of Baal cast down and the grove cut down?
options: They praised Gideon for his courage
They sought to identify who did it and condemned Gideon
questions.correctAnswer: They sought to identify who did it and condemned Gideon
questions.explanation: Judges 6:29-30 shows the men asking who was responsible, then demanding that Gideon be brought out to die for destroying Baal's altar and grove.

questions.question: What challenge did Joash present to those who wanted to kill Gideon?
options: He said Gideon must leave the city
He asked if anyone could plead for Baal to defend himself
He called for a council to decide
questions.correctAnswer: He asked if anyone could plead for Baal to defend himself
questions.explanation: Judges 6:31 records Joash challenging the accusers to plead for Baal since one had thrown down his altar, implying Baal's inability to defend himself.

questions.question: What new name was given to Gideon and what was its significance?
options: Jerubbaal, meaning 'Let Baal plead against him'
questions.correctAnswer: Jerubbaal, meaning 'Let Baal plead against him'
questions.explanation: Judges 6:32 states that Gideon was called Jerubbaal, signifying that Baal must contend with him because Gideon had destroyed his altar, symbolizing confrontation with idolatry.

questions.question: What does Judges 6:26 promise will happen if Gideon obeys the LORD's command to build an altar and offer a burnt sacrifice?
options: The LORD will bless Gideon's family
God's presence will confirm His acceptance of Gideon
questions.correctAnswer: God's presence will confirm His acceptance of Gideon
questions.explanation: Judges 6:25-26 describe the LORD commanding Gideon to build an altar and offer a sacrifice, implying that obedience will result in God's acceptance and favor, which is corroborated by the earlier divine signs in verses 19-21.

questions.question: True or False: Gideon was confident and proud of his family's status when called by God to save Israel.
questions.correctAnswer: False
questions.explanation: Judges 6:15 shows Gideon expressing humility and low regard for his own status, saying his family is poor and he is the least in his father's house, reflecting his initial lack of confidence.

questions.question: True or False: The men of the city wanted to kill Gideon for destroying the altar of Baal and the grove.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 6:30 records that the men of the city demanded Joash bring out Gideon to be put to death because of his destruction of Baal's altar and grove.

hard.title: Judges Chapter 6 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Judges Chapter 6.

questions.question: Who did the men of the city want Joash to bring out to be put to death?
questions.correctAnswer: Gideon
questions.explanation: Judges 6:30 states the men of the city said to Joash, 'Bring out thy son, that he may die,' referring to Gideon, because he had cast down the altar of Baal.

questions.question: What was the reason given by the men of the city for wanting Gideon dead?
options: For casting down the altar of Baal and cutting down the grove
For hiding wheat from the Midianites
questions.correctAnswer: For casting down the altar of Baal and cutting down the grove
questions.explanation: Judges 6:30 clearly states that Gideon was targeted because he cast down Baal's altar and cut down the grove next to it.

questions.question: What challenge did Joash present to those who wanted to punish Gideon?
options: To prove Gideon was a spy
To plead for Baal, to save him
To build a new altar for Baal
questions.correctAnswer: To plead for Baal, to save him
questions.explanation: Judges 6:31 shows Joash saying, 'Will ye plead for Baal? will ye save him? he that will plead for him, let him be put to death whilst it is yet morning: if he be a god, let him plead for himself.'

questions.question: What new name was given to Gideon and what does it mean?
questions.correctAnswer: Jerubbaal, meaning 'Baal pleads against him'
questions.explanation: Judges 6:32 states Gideon was called Jerubbaal because he threw down Baal's altar, literally meaning 'Let Baal plead against him.'

questions.question: Where did the Midianites and their allies pitch their camp against Israel?
questions.correctAnswer: Valley of Jezreel
questions.explanation: Judges 6:33 records that the Midianites and allies pitched in the valley of Jezreel to attack Israel.

questions.question: What significant event happened to Gideon that empowered him to gather followers?
options: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him
He built an altar to Baal
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of the LORD came upon him
questions.explanation: Judges 6:34 says the Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon, empowering him to blow a trumpet and gather supporters.

questions.question: Which tribes did Gideon send messengers to in order to gather support besides Manasseh?
questions.correctAnswer: Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali
questions.explanation: Judges 6:35 states that messengers were sent to Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, who came to join Gideon.

questions.question: What was Gideon's first sign to confirm God would save Israel by his hand?
options: Dew on a fleece only, with the ground dry
questions.correctAnswer: Dew on a fleece only, with the ground dry
questions.explanation: Judges 6:37-38 describe Gideon placing a fleece on the floor and asking for dew to be on it only, confirming God's promise.

questions.question: What did Gideon ask God to do for his second sign involving the fleece?
options: Make the fleece dry and the ground covered with dew
Make the fleece glow with fire
Make the fleece grow in size
Make the ground shake around him
questions.correctAnswer: Make the fleece dry and the ground covered with dew
questions.explanation: Judges 6:39-40 records Gideon's request for the fleece to be dry and the ground to have dew as a second confirmation, which God granted.

questions.question: True or False: Gideon was afraid to destroy the altar of Baal during the day because of his fear of his father's household and the men of the city.
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 6:27 explains Gideon did the task at night because he feared his father's household and the men of the city.

questions.question: True or False: The altar Gideon built after seeing the angel of the LORD was named Jehovahshalom, meaning 'The LORD is my peace.'
questions.correctAnswer: True
questions.explanation: Judges 6:24 states Gideon built an altar called Jehovahshalom, meaning 'The LORD is peace.'

questions.question: Which Old Testament book most closely parallels the theme of testing God with signs as seen in Gideon's fleece episode?
questions.correctAnswer: Isaiah
questions.explanation: Isaiah 7:10-14 records King Ahaz being offered a sign from God, paralleling Gideon's request for a sign—both reflecting the theme of divine confirmation.

questions.question: What literary device is predominantly used in the narrative of Gideon's calling and signs, especially in the fleece episodes?
questions.correctAnswer: Inclusio
questions.explanation: The fleece episodes in Judges 6:37-40 act as an inclusio, framing Gideon's call with divine signs that confirm God's presence and promise of deliverance.

questions.question: What is the Hebrew meaning of the name 'Jerubbaal' given to Gideon?
questions.correctAnswer: Let Baal contend
questions.explanation: Jerubbaal combines Hebrew roots meaning 'let Baal contend' or 'Baal will plead,' reflecting Gideon's conflict with Baal worship (Judges 6:32).

questions.question: How does the episode of Gideon's destruction of Baal's altar fulfill or develop the earlier theme of Israel's apostasy and idolatry?
options: It shows Israel's return to Baal worship
It symbolizes the rejection of false gods and restoration of Yahweh worship
It encourages syncretism of Baal and Yahweh
It depicts the triumph of Midianites over Israel
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the rejection of false gods and restoration of Yahweh worship
questions.explanation: Judges 6:25-32 narrate Gideon's destruction of Baal's altar, symbolizing Israel's breaking from idolatry and returning to worship of Yahweh, consistent with earlier admonitions in the book.

theological.title: Judges Chapter 6 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Judges Chapter 6 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What reason does Judges 6:1 give for the LORD delivering Israel into the hand of Midian for seven years?
options: The children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD
The children of Israel worshipped Baal
The Midianites were stronger in battle
questions.correctAnswer: The children of Israel did evil in the sight of the LORD
questions.explanation: Judges 6:1 explicitly states that Israel's evil in the sight of the LORD resulted in their being delivered into Midian's hand.

questions.question: According to Judges 6:12, what title does the angel of the LORD give to Gideon?
options: The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour
Servant of the Most High God
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD is with thee, thou mighty man of valour
questions.explanation: Judges 6:12 records the angel of the LORD addressing Gideon as 'thou mighty man of valour,' highlighting God's empowerment.

questions.question: What is Gideon's initial response to the angel's greeting in Judges 6:13, reflecting his doubt about God's presence?
options: ‘If the LORD be with us, why then is all this befallen us?’
‘I am ready to fight the Midianites’
‘Send me a sign to prove it’
questions.correctAnswer: ‘If the LORD be with us, why then is all this befallen us?’
questions.explanation: Judges 6:13 shows Gideon's doubt and confusion over Israel’s suffering despite God's promises, questioning God's presence.

questions.question: What divine assurance does God give to Gideon in Judges 6:16 about his mission?
options: Surely I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite the Midianites as one man
You will have many warriors with you
The Midianites will surrender without a fight
You must rely on your own strength
questions.correctAnswer: Surely I will be with thee, and thou shalt smite the Midianites as one man
questions.explanation: Judges 6:16 promises God's presence and power to enable Gideon to defeat Midian alone, emphasizing divine strength.

questions.question: What doctrinal truth about God's faithfulness is demonstrated by the sign of fire consuming the offering in Judges 6:21?
options: God confirms His presence and acceptance of worship
God hides His presence from sinners
questions.correctAnswer: God confirms His presence and acceptance of worship
questions.explanation: In Judges 6:21, the fire consuming the offering signifies God’s acceptance and confirmation of His messenger's divine authority.

questions.question: How does Judges 6:24 reflect the attribute of God known as 'Jehovahshalom'?
options: God is the source of peace
questions.correctAnswer: God is the source of peace
questions.explanation: Judges 6:24 records Gideon naming an altar 'Jehovahshalom,' meaning 'The LORD is peace,' highlighting God's peace-bringing nature.

questions.question: What theological significance does Gideon's act of destroying Baal's altar and the grove in Judges 6:25-27 convey?
options: The rejection of idolatry and exclusive worship of Yahweh
The establishment of a new religion
questions.correctAnswer: The rejection of idolatry and exclusive worship of Yahweh
questions.explanation: Judges 6:25-27 shows Gideon's obedience to God's command to destroy idolatrous sites, reinforcing monotheistic worship.

questions.question: According to Judges 6:31-32, what new name was given to Gideon and what does it signify about the spiritual conflict?
options: Jerubbaal, meaning 'Let Baal plead against him'
questions.correctAnswer: Jerubbaal, meaning 'Let Baal plead against him'
questions.explanation: Judges 6:31-32 records Gideon being called Jerubbaal, symbolizing the confrontation between Yahweh and Baal worship.

questions.question: How does Judges 6:33-35 illustrate the theme of divine empowerment in Israel’s deliverance?
options: The Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon, and he gathered an army
Israel defeats Midian by their own strength
questions.correctAnswer: The Spirit of the LORD came upon Gideon, and he gathered an army
questions.explanation: Judges 6:34-35 shows God’s Spirit empowering Gideon to lead Israel, underscoring divine enablement over human effort.

questions.question: What theological lesson is conveyed by Gideon's request for a sign using the fleece in Judges 6:36-40?
options: God graciously accommodates human doubt by providing confirmation
God demands absolute faith without any signs
Faith is irrelevant in God's plan
questions.correctAnswer: God graciously accommodates human doubt by providing confirmation
questions.explanation: Judges 6:36-40 reveal God’s patience with Gideon’s need for assurance, illustrating divine grace in human weakness.

questions.question: What combined doctrinal insight about Israel’s sin and God’s deliverance is revealed by Judges 6:1 and Judges 6:6?
options: Israel’s evil leads to oppression, but their cry to God initiates deliverance
Israel is always victorious without repentance
God abandons Israel permanently after sin
Deliverance depends solely on military strength
questions.correctAnswer: Israel’s evil leads to oppression, but their cry to God initiates deliverance
questions.explanation: Judges 6:1 shows Israel’s sin causing oppression; 6:6 reveals their cry to God, highlighting repentance as the path to salvation.

questions.question: What does the interaction between God and Gideon in Judges 6:14 and 6:16 teach about divine calling and human adequacy?
options: God calls despite human weakness and promises His presence for success
Only the strongest humans are chosen by God
questions.correctAnswer: God calls despite human weakness and promises His presence for success
questions.explanation: Judges 6:14 and 6:16 show God commissioning Gideon, who feels inadequate, assuring him of divine presence and power.

questions.question: Sceptics claim that God’s sending an angel to Gideon in Judges 6:11-12 is merely a mythological story with no theological value. What does Judges 6:11-12 actually teach about God’s interaction with humanity?
options: God actively initiates personal encounters to call and empower His servants
God is distant and uninvolved in human affairs
Miraculous appearances are only symbolic stories
God works only through human armies
questions.correctAnswer: God actively initiates personal encounters to call and empower His servants
questions.explanation: Judges 6:11-12 presents God’s angelic visitation as a real divine initiative to call Gideon, demonstrating God’s personal involvement.

questions.question: What attribute of God is demonstrated in Judges 6:9-10 where God reminds Israel of His past deliverances and commands them to fear Him, not the Amorite gods?
options: God’s sovereignty over history and His demand for exclusive worship
God’s limitation to only one nation
questions.correctAnswer: God’s sovereignty over history and His demand for exclusive worship
questions.explanation: Judges 6:9-10 emphasizes God's sovereign acts in history and His call for Israel’s exclusive fear and obedience.

questions.question: How does the narrative in Judges 6:28-30 illustrate the social cost of faithfulness to God in a corrupted society?
options: Gideon faced death threats from his community for destroying Baal's altar
Gideon was immediately honored and praised
questions.correctAnswer: Gideon faced death threats from his community for destroying Baal's altar
questions.explanation: Judges 6:28-30 shows Gideon’s risking life due to opposition from his people, demonstrating faithful obedience’s cost.
